newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.

text.p: In the South, rice prices were steady to $0.50 higher. Long grain milled rice prices were selling mostly at $20.00 per cwt.; Medium grain traded mostly at $18.00-19.00; Second heads were steady and Brewers remain in very tight supply with few quotes at $14.50-15.50.
Rice by-products were uneven, bran was steady to $2.00 higher, millfeed was steady to $2.00 lower, USDA said.
In California, rice prices were steady to 50 cents lower, instances $1.00 lower, with Medium grain selling mostly at $19.00-19.50 with some discounts down to $18.00. Rice bran was $2.00-15.00 higher.

California rice ship loadings For the week ending January 18, 1997, there were no ship loadings reported. Inspections of California rice for export There were no inspections for the week ending January 18, 1997.
The yearly total since October 1, 1996 is 4,081,401 cwt compared to 2,443,152 cwt a year ago.

Domestic shipment: Offers, FOB mills, milled rice, dollars per cwt, bagged. (All milled rice grade 2 not to exceed 4 percent brokens, except California grade 1. All second heads grade 4 or better, Second heads and Brewers bulk.)
